title: The whisper
hookLine: Shaytan whispers to them both and they eat, and their shame appears (7:20–22)

cards: It's two in the morning and you can't sleep. A voice in your head starts up. It never shouts.
Just reasonable. One more episode won't hurt. You deserve that.
Or the other kind: they were laughing at you, weren't they. You'll never be good enough. It sounds exactly like your own voice.
That's what makes it work. Today, the garden has everything, and one tree, and then someone starts to talk. Not with a shout, or a threat.

teach.b: Surah seven, verse twenty: “Then Satan whispered to them.” The Arabic verb is waswasa, and listen to it: was-was. The word itself whispers.
It's the sound of lips close to an ear. What did he say? He didn't say, disobey God.
He renamed the tree. In another surah, he calls it the tree of immortality, and a kingdom that never wears out. Your Lord only forbade it, he says, so you wouldn't become angels, or live forever.
Then he swore to them that he was a sincere adviser. The forbidden thing, dressed up as a gift. A limit, dressed up as God holding out on you.

And they ate, and at once their shame appeared to them, and they began covering themselves with leaves of the garden. In surah seven, the whisper, the eating and the shame are all told in the Arabic dual: the two of them.
The Qur'an doesn't pin it on the woman.
The whisper came to both, and both ate. The Qur'an's last surah names this voice: in Pickthall's words, “the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind.”
In Arabic, al-waswas al-khannas, the whisperer who slinks back. Many commentators explain: it retreats when God is remembered, and comes back when you forget.
And a hadith in Bukhari brings real relief: God has forgiven people what their own souls whisper to them, as long as they don't act on it or say it. The whisper isn't the wrong. Following it is.
So the thought at two in the morning isn't a verdict on you. It's just a voice. And not every voice is yours.

how: When Muslims feel an evil or anxious whisper, many say a'udhu billahi mina sh-shaytani r-rajim, I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, and recite the last two surahs, al-Falaq and an-Nas.

o: a shouted order to break God's law outright
a quiet whisper that pulls you toward wrong
a guilty feeling that comes after a mistake

games.q: what's inside the whisper — tap the pairs.
p: the whisper; the word itself whispers
the whisperer's new name for it

s: in the Qur'an, the woman tempted Adam
in surah seven the whisper came to both of them, and both ate. the Qur'an doesn't pin it on her.
the whisperer told them to disobey God outright
he renamed the tree: immortality, a kingdom that never wears out. the limit dressed up as a gift.
a hadith says God forgives what the soul whispers, if it isn't acted on
as long as people don't act on it or say it (Bukhari).

games.q: you're the whisperer. you want them to eat from the one tree. what's your best move?
o: rename the tree and swear you're only trying to help.
games.why: he called it the tree of immortality and swore he was a sincere adviser. the forbidden, dressed as a gift.

practice: Listen to your own mind; thoughts will come, some kind, some sharp, some selling you something.
Don't argue with any of them, but when one pulls at you, a craving, a cruel line about yourself, a grudge, label it softly, whisper, and let it pass like a car going by outside.
If you pray, you can say a'udhu billah, I seek refuge in God, the words Muslims use when a whisper comes.

wordCard.voice: Waswas. The whisper: a quiet voice that renames the tree and sounds like your own. The whisperer slinks back when God is remembered.

orig.note: Arabic: the whisperer, the whispering; the sound of the word imitates a whisper.

carryVoice: Your line: not every voice is yours. The story isn't over yet. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind

sources.ref: Qur'an 7:20–22; 20:120–121 (the tree renamed; the oath; the eating and the leaves)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2528 (what the soul whispers is forgiven unless acted on or spoken)
